title: How the parties would investigate Oct 7
question: Who should investigate October 7?

stances.label: An independent inquiry, form not set
A state commission under the 1968 law

note: Party answers to a Ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth survey of all parties (Oct 4, 2026). Likud gave no official response; its row is Ynet's account of its bill for a 'national' commission. Otzma Yehudit, Shas and United Torah Judaism declined to respond; the Shas and UTJ rows add the coalition bill they backed at its first reading (Times of Israel, July 7, 2026). No published position found for Noam (checked October 2026).

rows.text: No official response. Likud "later sought to advance a private bill creating an alternative body described as a 'national' commission, but the effort was not completed before the end of the Knesset term" (Ynet's account).

Religious Zionism: "supports establishing a national, independent, genuine and fair commission of inquiry... We will under no circumstances support a 'state' commission of inquiry..." Zehut, its list partner: "a neutral commission with unlimited powers... The coalition and opposition will appoint its members equally."

"Immediately upon the establishment of the next government, a commission of inquiry will be formed... a secret vote in the new Knesset to appoint the commission's chair and deputy chair, retired judges who will select the remaining members of the commission."

"The first decision of our government will be to establish a state commission of inquiry into the Oct. 7 massacre. The commission will be established in accordance with Section 1 of the Commissions of Inquiry Law, 1968."
"We will establish a state commission of inquiry in accordance with the law within the first five minutes of the first government meeting, on the day the government is sworn in."

"Establishing a state commission of inquiry will be the first decision the party advances in the next government... The commission's members will be appointed by the president of the Supreme Court, as required under the Commissions of Inquiry Law, 1968."
"We support establishing a state commission of inquiry exactly according to the existing law in the State of Israel. This will be the first decision we make in the government we establish."
"Blue and White has supported and continues to support establishing an independent and impartial state commission of inquiry into Oct. 7... the current mechanism is a good one."
"We support a state commission of inquiry. It is preferable to reach broad agreement on its composition. Who should appoint it? The Supreme Court, with a preference for Sohlberg."

"We support establishing a state commission of inquiry under existing law, headed by a Supreme Court justice and appointed by the president of the Supreme Court." Wants its mandate to include "the policies of occupation, blockade and rejection of peace under Netanyahu governments."
A commission "is not currently at the center of Ra'am's agenda," but "there is a need for a comprehensive, independent and impartial investigation of the events of Oct. 7."

Declined Ynet's survey. On the record: backed the coalition's bill for an Oct 7 panel appointed through the Knesset, not a state commission, which passed its first reading 59 to 0 on Jul 7, 2026, with the opposition boycotting.
rows.source: Ynet, Oct 4, 2026; Times of Israel, Jul 7, 2026
